decisions.rationale: Pelipper at 4% HP must protect or KO Lucario. Lucario outspeeds and threatens Pelipper, but Pelipper's Hydro Pump in Rain cleanly KOes Lucario (69.5-136.6% HP). However, Rotom-Mow outspeeds and can finish Pelipper. Wait, if Lucario uses Protect or ExtremeSpeed, Hydro Pump into Lucario gets the KO if Lucario doesn't Protect. If Lucario Protects, Pelipper faints to Rotom. But Protect on Pelipper blocks Lucario's attack and Rotom's attack if they target Pelipper, though Pelipper is at 4% and needs to pressure. Let's look at Hydro Pump into Lucario: Hydro Pump has 80% accuracy and OHKOs Lucario.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper is the last foe at 4% HP. Rotom Thunderbolt is 4x and a guaranteed KO (52.7-127.4% > 4%); Lucario Extreme Speed also KOs (19.8-44.4%). If it Protects we still win next turn. Series clinched 2-0.

reflections.summary: We lost the game and series (0-2) primarily because Rotom-Mow completely dismantled our rain core. Rotom's 4x resistance to Water and super-effective Leaf Storm/Thunderbolt effortlessly neutralized Mega Swampert, Basculegion, and Pelipper, while Slowbro's Protect stalls and Lucario's offensive pressure cleaned up the remaining threats. Our roster selection lacked a reliable offensive answer to Grass-types like Rotom-Mow, making the Drizzle strategy a liability rather than an advantage.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, I would register Altaria or Feraligatr from the left-behind pool to better handle Grass-types like Rotom-Mow. I would also reconsider bringing Mega Swampert against opponents with multiple Water-resisting pivots and Grass coverage, opting instead for a more balanced team composition.
reflections.notebook: Opponent utilized Rotom-Mow as a hard counter to rain strategies, leveraging Leaf Storm and Thunderbolt alongside Slowbro's Regenerator/Protect utility and Lucario's priority/Close Combat pressure. Pelipper and rain sweepers struggle heavily when confronted with Levitate Grass-types and reliable defensive stalling.

reflections.summary: Game 2 and the series (2-0) were won because the four brought (Rotom-Mow, Slowbro, Lucario, Gengar) perfectly countered the opponent’s Water-rain core: Rotom-Mow’s Leaf Storm/Thunderbolt super-effectively erased Swampert, Basculegion and Pelipper, while Lucario’s Close Combat/Extreme Speed OHKOed Archaludon and finished Pelipper. Not Mega-evolving Gengar was correct given Basculegion’s speed/threat. Between-game adjustments (keeping Rotom-Lucario offensive core, using Slowbro as Protect pivot, holding Gengar unmega as backup) helped, not backfired, sealing the sweep. Prep was largely right: the registered six (Mega Gengar, Garchomp, Empoleon, Slowbro, Lucario, Rotom-Mow) contained the key counters; left-behind Pokémon were unnecessary. Only minor oversight was Slowbro’s fragility as sole pivot vs Basculegion’s Last Respects, but it did not cost the game.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series vs this opponent, retain Rotom-Mow + Lucario as anchors and still avoid Mega Gengar while Basculegion lives. Consider swapping Slowbro for Garchomp or Empoleon if Raichu/Tsareena appear, since Slowbro’s Protect stall failed to survive Basculegion and adds little offense. Keep Grass/Electric coverage and lead Rotom-Mow into Pelipper/Swampert leads.
